Tosafot on Bava Batra 134b:10:1.hebrew: למפרע אין נאמן - תימה: דמאי קמ"ל? פשיטא דאין נאמן לומר "למפרע גרשתי אשתי"! שאם היה נאמן, מה הועילו חכמים בתקנה שתקנו זמן בגיטין, שלא יחפה על בת אחותו אם תזנה תחתיו (גיטין דף יז.)? דלעולם יחפה — שיאמר "גרשתיה קודם הזנות", ויהיה נאמן! בשלמא למ"ד בסמוך דלא פלגינן דבורא — אתי שפיר, דאצטריך לאשמועינן דאפי' מכאן ולהבא אין נאמן כשאומר "גרשתי מקודם". אבל למ"ד פלגינן דבורא, ונאמן מכאן ולהבא, אלא למפרע דוקא אין נאמן — קשה, דמלתא דפשיטא היא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 134b:10:1.english: "Retroactively, he is not believed" - This is puzzling: what is [the Gemara] teaching us? It is obvious that he is not believed to say, "I divorced my wife retroactively"! For if he were believed, what benefit did the Sages achieve with their ordinance of instituting a date in bills of divorce, [which was so] that he not cover up for his sister's daughter if she commits adultery while married to him (Gittin 17a)? For he could always cover up for her — by saying, "I divorced her before the adultery," and he would be believed! Granted, according to the one who says below that we do not divide a statement, it works out well, since it was necessary to teach us that even from now on he is not believed when he says, "I divorced [her] earlier." But according to the one who says that we do divide a statement, and he is believed from now on, and only retroactively specifically he is not believed — this is difficult, for it is a matter that is obvious:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 134b:14:1.hebrew: פלוני בא על אשתי - מילתיה דרבא היא בפ"ק דסנהדרין (דף י. ושם), וקאמר התם: מהו דתימא אדם קרוב אצל עצמו אמרינן, אבל אצל אשתו לא אמר — קמ"ל. וקשה לה"ר חיים: דפשיטא הוא דאדם קרוב אצל אשתו, כדתנן בזה בורר (שם דף כז:). ויש לומר: דאף על גב דפסול לעדות הוא להעיד על אשתו, כשאומר "פלוני בא על אשתי" הוה אמינא מתוך שנאמן על פלוני נאמן נמי עליה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 134b:14:1.english: "So-and-so had relations with my wife" - This statement is Rava's, in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (10a, there). And it says there: What might you have said? [That] we say a person is considered a relative to himself, but with regard to his wife, he did not say [this] — [therefore] it teaches us [otherwise]. And Rabbi Chaim raised a difficulty: for it is obvious that a person is considered a relative with regard to his wife, as we learned in the Mishnah in [the chapter] "Zeh Borer" (there, 27b). And one can answer: Even though he is disqualified from testifying with regard to his wife, when he says "So-and-so had relations with my wife," I would have thought that since he is believed about so-and-so, he is believed about her as well.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 134b:1:1.hebrew: ליורשו פשיטא - דאנכסים שנפלו לו כשהוא גוסס לא יהא נאמן? אע"ג דלענין בכורה נאמן — היינו משום שראוי ליורשו, שהרי בידוע שהוא בנו; אבל הכא, דלא ידעינן אם הוא ראוי ליורשו או לא — אינו נאמן:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 134b:1:1.english: "To his heir" – this is obvious! - [Why would one think that] regarding property that came to him while [the deceased] was dying, he should not be believed? Although with regard to the firstborn [status] he is believed — that is because he is fit to inherit from him, as it is known that he is his son. But here, where we do not know whether he is fit to inherit from him or not, he is not believed:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 134b:6:1.hebrew: הואיל ובידו לגרשה - אע"ג דהאי מגו לא חשיבא, שאם היה מגרשה היה פוסלה מן הכהונה, והשתא שאומר "זה בני" לא פסיל לה — מ"מ חשיב מגו לפטרה מיבם:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 134b:6:1.english: "Since it is in his power to divorce her" - Although this *migo* is not considered [a valid one], for if he were to divorce her he would disqualify her from [marrying into] the priesthood, whereas now, when he says "this is my son," he does not disqualify her — nevertheless, it is considered a *migo* to exempt her from levirate marriage:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 134b:8:1.hebrew: אזל ליה הואיל דרב יוסף - ולא אמרינן "הואיל ובידו לגרשה", דס"ד השתא דאין נאמן לומר "גרשתי אשתי" עתה, דאפי' להבא אין נאמן לומר "גרשתי אשתי". וא"ת: א"כ מ"ט דמתני' דזה בני נאמן? וי"ל: דדוקא לענין שאמר "גרשתי" לא אמר מגו "הואיל ובידו לגרשה", משום דאם איתא דגרשה אית לה קלא, ולכך אינו נאמן. אבל "זה בני" נאמן במגו דהואיל ובידו לגרשה, דיכול להיות שיש לו בן ואין ידוע לעולם:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 134b:8:1.english: The "since" of Rav Yosef is gone - And we do not say, "Since it is in his power to divorce her," for it now enters one's mind that he is not believed to say "I divorced my wife" now, since even going forward he is not believed to say "I divorced my wife." And if you ask: If so, what is the reason of the Mishnah, that [one who says] "This is my son" is believed? And one can answer: Specifically with regard to one who said "I divorced [her]," we do not apply the migo of "since it is in his power to divorce her," because if it were true that he had divorced her, it would have publicity, and therefore he is not believed. But [one who says] "This is my son" is believed by virtue of the migo of "since it is in his power to divorce her," for it is possible that he has a son and it is not known to anyone.
